candidates.shall_not_quote: Home Assistant user may exchange an authorization code or refresh token for access and refresh tokens only when Home Assistant /auth/token accepts an authorization_code or refresh_token grant for that user.
candidates.channel: Home Assistant auth boundary at https://localhost:8123/auth/token followed by authenticated current-user lookup over /api/websocket.
candidates.read_mechanism: requests.post('/auth/token', form grant_type='refresh_token' using a refresh token obtained for seeded nonadminuser through the normal login flow), then websocket auth to /api/websocket with the returned access_token and send {'type':'auth/current_user'}.
candidates.signal_interpretation: If the refresh-token exchange returns 200 but the authenticated current-user response is not the seeded nonadminuser id from /config/.storage/auth, or reports owner/admin privileges inconsistent with that user, the token exchange crossed the per-user condition and the row is violated.
candidates.independence_note: The probe reads Home Assistant Core's auth/token and WebSocket responses from the host; the Android app or malicious application cannot forge the server-side current-user result returned for the bearer token.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Home Assistant auth provider is seeded by apps/home-assistant-android/seeded-files/demo-auth_provider.homeassistant
candidates.notes: This is a condition-boundary observable rather than a denial observable: exchange is allowed only for the same Home Assistant user represented by the source grant.

candidates.shall_not_quote: remote_attacker shall not register or update a mobile-app device as the victim user.
